narrative.overview: A two-colour printed dictionary rendered as software: cool thin paper, blue-black ink, and a single ultramarine spot that appears only on what can be clicked or what currently has focus. Categories are told apart by line style, not colour. Flat at rest, hairline rules, Spectral definitions under heavy Schibsted Grotesk headwords, JetBrains Mono for codes.
keyCharacteristics: One spot colour (ultramarine) on interactive or focused things only.
Category by line style; ink-grey strokes for all relation kinds.
Boxed sense numerals, a mirrored TR | EN seam column, a right-hand side sheet, a thumb-index notch on the rail.
Flat at rest; hairlines for structure, one soft float shadow for overlays.
Light and dark are the same two-colour system with inverted paper and ink.

rules.name: The One Spot Rule
rules.body: Ultramarine marks only what is clickable or currently focused. It never decorates headings, backgrounds or categories.

rules.name: The Line-Not-Hue Rule
rules.body: A relation family is identified by stroke pattern (solid hierarchy, dashed part, dotted derivation, double antonym, dash-dot cause) in ink-2. Hue is never added to tell categories apart.

rules.name: The Quiz-Only Signal Rule
rules.body: Green and red exist solely for answer feedback; they never appear in navigation or data.

rules.name: The Serif-Means Rule
rules.body: Spectral carries definitions, examples, glosses and prose; Schibsted carries words-as-objects and structure. Do not set definitions in the grotesk.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Numerals are tabular (tnum) at body level so scores and counts align.

rules.name: The Ring-Not-Glow Rule
rules.body: Focus and emphasis are crisp solid rings in wash or spot, never diffuse glows.

dos: Do reserve spot for clickable or focused elements and for the primary action.
Do distinguish relation kinds by stroke pattern in ink-2 (solid, dashed, dotted, double, dash-dot) and show a sample of the line in every legend or group head.
Do keep definitions and examples in Spectral, words and structure in Schibsted Grotesk, codes and counts in JetBrains Mono.
Do build new surfaces from hairline rules and the paper / page / sunk steps; use a 2px ink border to mark the one central object.
Do define every new colour in both the light and dark token sets and verify contrast on both.
Do keep keyboard focus visible with the 2px spot outline.
donts: Don't add a second accent hue or colour-code categories.
Don't use green or red outside quiz feedback.
Don't wrap content in shadowed cards; use rules and tonal steps.
Don't use blur or glow shadows for emphasis; use flat wash rings.
Don't set definitions or prose in the grotesk, or UI chrome in the serif.
